# atlys

> A curated collection of 47 skills for AI coding agents — design taste, anti-slop writing, and engineering QA as drop-in playbooks.

Install: `npx skills add adiprmx/atlys`
Repo: https://github.com/adiprmx/atlys

## Skills

- [accessibility](design/accessibility/SKILL.md) (design): Quality assurance for web accessibility and usability, particularly for users with disabilities. Use when involved in any web project.
- [accessibility-testing](design/accessibility-testing/SKILL.md) (design): Use for testing the accessibility of a web project
- [brandkit](design/brandkit/SKILL.md) (design): 'Brand-kit image generation: logo systems, identity decks, and brand-guideline
- [brutalist-skill](design/brutalist-skill/SKILL.md) (design): Raw mechanical interfaces fusing Swiss typographic print with military
- [frontend-image-direction](design/frontend-image-direction/SKILL.md) (design): Section references, mobile screen concepts, and brand-consistent image
- [gpt-tasteskill](design/gpt-tasteskill/SKILL.md) (design): 'UX/UI plus advanced GSAP motion engineering: AIDA page structure, wide
- [image-to-code-skill](design/image-to-code-skill/SKILL.md) (design): Generates the design images first, analyzes them deeply, then implements
- [imagegen-frontend-mobile](design/imagegen-frontend-mobile/SKILL.md) (design): Mobile app screen concepts and flows (iOS/Android/cross-platform), presented
- [imagegen-frontend-web](design/imagegen-frontend-web/SKILL.md) (design): 'Generates conversion-aware website design references: one horizontal
- [impeccable-design](design/impeccable-design/SKILL.md) (design): "Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. Covers websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, app shells, components, forms, settings, onboarding, and empty states. Handles UX review, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, theming, anti-patterns, typography, fonts, spacing, layout, alignment, color, motion, micro-interactions, UX copy, error states, edge cases, i18n, and reusable design systems or tokens. Also use for bland designs that need to become bolder or more delightful, loud designs that should become quieter, live browser iteration on UI elements, or ambitious visual effects that should feel technically extraordinary. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks."
- [minimalist-skill](design/minimalist-skill/SKILL.md) (design): 'Clean editorial interfaces: warm monochrome, typographic contrast, flat
- [premium-frontend-engineering](design/premium-frontend-engineering/SKILL.md) (design): 'Hand-coded frontend: brief-driven design dials, bias-corrected typography
- [redesign-skill](design/redesign-skill/SKILL.md) (design): Upgrades existing websites and apps without breaking functionality. Audit-first;
- [soft-skill](design/soft-skill/SKILL.md) (design): 'Agency-grade polish: exact fonts, spacing, shadows, card structures,
- [stitch-skill](design/stitch-skill/SKILL.md) (design): Semantic design-system skill for Google Stitch. Generates agent-friendly
- [taste-skill](design/taste-skill/SKILL.md) (design): Anti-slop frontend for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. Reads
- [taste-skill-v1](design/taste-skill-v1/SKILL.md) (design): The original v1 of taste-skill, preserved for projects depending on its
- [antislop-code](writing/antislop-code/SKILL.md) (writing): "Code comment hygiene for AI coding agents: remove generic AI-slop comments, keep the valuable ones, never touch the code."
- [antislop-copywriting](writing/antislop-copywriting/SKILL.md) (writing): "Copy and text skill for antislop. Use when writing or editing prose: headlines, tone, CTAs, and anti-AI-writing patterns. Load with the core."
- [antislop-core](writing/antislop-core/SKILL.md) (writing): "Anti Slop: Rules for AI Coding Agents. The core filter. Load always to stop generic AI slop."
- [antislop-human](writing/antislop-human/SKILL.md) (writing): "Human and accessibility skill for antislop. Contrast, keyboard, focus, and states for real people. Includes the contrast checker."
- [antislop-layoutmobile](writing/antislop-layoutmobile/SKILL.md) (writing): "Mobile layout skill for antislop. Use for layouts that reflow across screen sizes, phone to desktop: grids, overflow, tap targets. Load with the core."
- [antislop-ui](writing/antislop-ui/SKILL.md) (writing): "UI and visual skill for antislop. Use when building or editing any interface: color, layout, components, motion. Load with the core."
- [avoid-ai-writing](writing/avoid-ai-writing/SKILL.md) (writing): "Avoid AI Writing: audit & rewrite untuk menghapus pola tulisan AI ('AI-isms'). Mode detect-only, edit-in-place, profil suara (casual/professional/technical/warm/blunt), dan pass iterasi-sampai-konvergen. Punya kontrak editing ketat: deteksi bukan vonis, temuan bukan edit otomatis. Dikalibrasi untuk Bahasa Inggris; untuk Bahasa Indonesia pakai sebagai panduan pola struktural."
- [crafting-effective-readmes](writing/crafting-effective-readmes/SKILL.md) (writing): Use when writing or improving README files. Not all READMEs are the same — provides templates and guidance matched to your audience and project type.
- [humanizer](writing/humanizer/SKILL.md) (writing): "Humanizer: ubah tulisan beraroma AI jadi terdengar seperti manusia tanpa mengubah isinya. Pakai saat mengedit/mereview prosa: deteksi pola AI (kontras not-X-but-Y, closer satu baris, triad paksa, dash berlebih, klaim bombastis, kata stok AI, bold dekoratif, sisa chat). Berbasis riset Wikipedia 'Signs of AI writing'. Cocok untuk copy Indonesia yang diterjemahkan/ditulis ulang dari pola Inggris."
- [no-ai-slop](writing/no-ai-slop/SKILL.md) (writing): "No AI Slop: edit draf jadi tajam dan manusiawi sambil menjaga suara penulis, atau deteksi pola AI-slop tanpa menulis ulang. Dua mode: Edit (minimum effective edit + What changed) dan Detect (sebut pola, kutip baris, beri fix singkat). Pakai saat user minta draf lebih jelas, lebih direct, lebih beropini, atau bertanya apakah tulisannya terdengar AI."
- [stop-slop](writing/stop-slop/SKILL.md) (writing): "Stop Slop: pangkas retorika & basa-basi AI dari prosa. 8 aturan inti (potong filler, hancurkan struktur formulaik, aktif, spesifik, variasi ritme) + daftar frasa yang wajib dibuang + cek kilat + skor 1-10 per dimensi. Pakai saat menulis, mengedit, atau mereview teks agar langsung ke poin."
- [writing-quality](writing/writing-quality/SKILL.md) (writing): Apply on every turn that drafts or edits human-facing prose, even when writing is not the main task. Covers chat replies, explanations, emails, documents, pull request descriptions, issue comments, and review reports. Keep writing natural, direct, plain, and aligned with the user's voice. Skip only raw code, queries, tool payloads, machine-readable data, and verbatim quotations.
- [android-architecture](engineering/android-architecture/SKILL.md) (engineering): Expert guidance on setting up and maintaining a modern Android application architecture using Clean Architecture and Hilt. Use this when asked about project structure, module setup, or dependency injection.
- [android-compose-performance](engineering/android-compose-performance/SKILL.md) (engineering): Audit and improve Jetpack Compose runtime performance from code review and architecture. Use when asked to diagnose slow rendering, janky scrolling, excessive recompositions, or performance issues in Compose UI.
- [android-testing](engineering/android-testing/SKILL.md) (engineering): Comprehensive testing strategy involving Unit, Integration, Hilt, and Screenshot tests.
- [batch-run-integrity](engineering/batch-run-integrity/SKILL.md) (engineering): 'Keeps long multi-chunk batch jobs honest and resumable: incremental
- [c4-architecture](engineering/c4-architecture/SKILL.md) (engineering): Generate architecture documentation using C4 model Mermaid diagrams. Use when asked to create architecture diagrams, document system architecture, visualize software structure, create C4 diagrams, or generate context/container/component/deployment diagrams. Triggers include "architecture diagram", "C4 diagram", "system context", "container diagram", "component diagram", "deployment diagram", "document architecture", "visualize architecture".
- [database-schema-designer](engineering/database-schema-designer/SKILL.md) (engineering): Design robust, scalable database schemas for SQL and NoSQL databases. Provides normalization guidelines, indexing strategies, migration patterns, constraint design, and performance optimization. Ensures data integrity, query performance, and maintainable data models.
- [docker-build-strategies](engineering/docker-build-strategies/SKILL.md) (engineering): Use this skill when writing, reviewing, or optimizing Dockerfiles, even if the user just says their image is too large, their build is slow, or they need to harden a container for production. Covers multi-stage builds, layer caching, .dockerignore, non-root users, and image size optimization.
- [docker-compose-patterns](engineering/docker-compose-patterns/SKILL.md) (engineering): Use this skill when creating, modifying, or debugging Docker Compose configurations, even if the user just says they need to wire services together, add a database to their stack, or set up a local development environment with multiple containers. Covers service definitions, health checks, dependency ordering, volumes, networks, environment variables, and development overrides.
- [docker-destructive-guardrails](engineering/docker-destructive-guardrails/SKILL.md) (engineering): Use this skill before running, or recommending, any Docker command that deletes, wipes, resets, or otherwise irreversibly changes state — even if the user just says to "clean up", "clear the cache", "start fresh", "wipe everything", "nuke it", "reset", "force remove", or "tear down" Docker resources. Covers generic Docker CLI destructive operations not owned by a more specific skill — `docker rm`, `docker rm -f`, `docker container prune`, `docker kill`, `docker system prune`, `docker rmi`/`docker image rm`, `docker image prune -a`, `docker network rm`, `docker network prune`, `docker builder prune`, `docker buildx rm`, `docker context rm`, and standalone (non-Compose) `docker volume rm`/`docker volume prune`. Also indexes destructive commands owned by other Docker skills (Compose, sandbox, Desktop). Core rule — state exactly what will be lost and get explicit confirmation first, except narrow, low-friction Tier 1 container cleanup.
- [docker-project-foundations](engineering/docker-project-foundations/SKILL.md) (engineering): Use this skill when setting up, initializing, or Dockerizing a project, even if the user doesn't explicitly mention Docker but describes a need for containerized local development, adding a database or cache dependency, or running services without host-level installs. Covers Dockerfile, compose.yaml, and .dockerignore creation with Docker best practices.
- [go-service-scaffolder](engineering/go-service-scaffolder/SKILL.md) (engineering): Scaffold a production-ready Go HTTP service with OpenTelemetry observability, TLS, lifecycle management, Dockerfile, GitHub Actions CI/CD, and golangci-lint. Use when creating or regenerating a full Go service skeleton (project layout, config package, server package, CI workflows, and container build files).
- [golang-concurrency](engineering/golang-concurrency/SKILL.md) (engineering): "Golang concurrency design — goroutine lifecycle and leak prevention, channels and `select`, channel ownership and direction, `sync.Mutex`/`RWMutex`/`sync.Map`/`sync.Once`/atomics, `errgroup`, `singleflight`, worker pools, and fan-out/fan-in pipelines. Use when writing or reviewing concurrent Go code, when choosing between channels and mutexes, when protecting a shared map or counter, or when a goroutine has no clear exit. Not for defensive coding unrelated to concurrency such as nil panics, slice aliasing, or numeric overflow (→ See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-safety` skill), and not for debugging a specific hung, crashing, or racing program after the fact (→ See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-troubleshooting` skill)."
- [golang-error-handling](engineering/golang-error-handling/SKILL.md) (engineering): "Idiomatic Golang error handling — creation, wrapping with %w, errors.Is/As, errors.Join, custom error types, sentinel errors, panic/recover, the single handling rule, structured logging with slog, HTTP request logging middleware, and samber/oops for production errors. Built to make logs usable at scale with log aggregation 3rd-party tools. Apply when creating, wrapping, inspecting, or logging errors in Go code. For samber/oops specifics → See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-samber-oops` skill; for slog handler ecosystem → See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-samber-slog` skill."
- [golang-testing](engineering/golang-testing/SKILL.md) (engineering): "Production-ready Golang tests — table-driven tests, testify suites and mocks, parallel tests, fuzzing, fixtures, goroutine leak detection with goleak, snapshot testing, code coverage, integration tests, idiomatic test naming. Use when writing or reviewing Go tests, choosing a testing approach, setting up Go test CI, or debugging flaky/slow tests. For testify-specific APIs see `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-stretchr-testify`; for measurement methodology see `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-benchmark`."
- [hexagonal-python](engineering/hexagonal-python/SKILL.md) (engineering): Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters) with Domain-Driven Design for Python backends built with FastAPI or Flask, SQLAlchemy and pytest. Use it to design, implement, review, refactor or migrate Python server-side code - REST APIs, use cases, aggregates, value objects, repositories, unit of work, domain events and outbox, bounded contexts, error handling, idempotency, pagination and tests per boundary. Trigger it when the project has pyproject.toml, requirements*.txt or setup.py and the user mentions hexagonal, ports and adapters, clean architecture, DDD, layers, use cases, repositories, services, a fat route or view, decoupling from FastAPI, Flask or the database, or how to structure a Python API, even if they never say "hexagonal". Also use it for architecture, SOLID or testability reviews of Python backend code. Not for other languages - use the matching hexagonal-<language> skill.
- [intent-pattern-qa](engineering/intent-pattern-qa/SKILL.md) (engineering): Catches silent regex-pattern death (patterns that compile but never match)
- [output-skill](engineering/output-skill/SKILL.md) (engineering): Overrides default LLM truncation behavior. Enforces complete code generation,
- [worker-resource-budgeting](engineering/worker-resource-budgeting/SKILL.md) (engineering): Budgets RAM before fanning out parallel workers, so verification workers
